A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DICE-RL work, with readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. V1 Appendices A-C are retained as v2 Appendices B-D, alongside a new Appendix A.

before.justification: V1 reports original Robomimic experiments, three real-robot manipulation experiments, robustness analyses, and extensive appendix ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds LIBERO-10 multitask experiments using a multitask BC policy and the pretrained π0 model.

M1.justification: V2 adds a specific π0 integration: image and language tokens produce an action-free, pooled latent for the residual actor and critic, while base actions come from separate π0 inference. This is a limited input/representation adaptation; Algorithm 1, residual learning objectives, filtering, and action selection remain unchanged.

E1.justification: New Appendix A adds LIBERO-10 and joint multitask learning, including language-conditioned π0 experiments. This substantially extends the evaluated task requirements beyond v1's individual Robomimic and real-robot tasks, all of which are retained.

E2.justification: The original comparisons with IBRL, DPPO, EXPO, DSRL, and ResFit remain intact. The new LIBERO experiments reuse DSRL and pretrained-policy comparisons; π0 is an additional backbone, not a new competing finetuning method. The expanded ResFit description does not establish a changed implementation.

E3.justification: Appendix A introduces a substantial multitask experimental design: BC pretraining on 500 demonstrations across ten tasks, random task selection during online collection, and task-averaged evaluation with 100 rollouts per task in Figure 10. The π0 experiment adds supervised finetuning with 30 demonstrations per task before RL. These are additional protocols; the original experimental settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The component ablations, hyperparameter sweeps, pretraining analyses, trajectory-divergence analysis, and action-noise tests are retained. V1 Figures 10-19 become v2 Figures 14-23 with unchanged plotted content. The new LIBERO per-task curves provide benchmark results rather than distinct ablations or robustness analyses.

E5.justification: Five-seed averaging and variability reporting for the original comparisons and ablations remain unchanged. Appendix A specifies evaluation rollouts but introduces no explicit new seed count, significance test, or uncertainty-estimation procedure; the original five-seed statements cannot automatically be extended to these additions.

E6.justification: V2 Figures 10-13 add aggregate and per-task learning curves for both LIBERO settings. They report better aggregate sample efficiency than DSRL and improved π0 performance following RL. These substantially expand the reported evidence under new conditions; the original benchmark, real-robot, and ablation results are retained rather than improved or replaced.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, objectives, filter definition, finetunability metrics, trajectory-divergence measure, and flow-matching equations are unchanged. V2 adds no theorem, proof, formal assumption, or mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, three introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same substantive wording and claims about stable, sample-efficient finetuning and distribution sharpening/contraction. The new experiments supply broader evidence without revising these core claims.

C2.justification: The explanations of distribution sharpening, contraction, and hyperparameter effects remain unchanged, as does the limitation to robustness against small on-trajectory perturbations rather than claimed out-of-distribution gains. Figure 7's caption correction aligns it with the already-existing graph and discussion.

D1.justification: Appendix A documents the π0 interface: a forward pass stopping before action generation, averaging image/text token outputs into a 2048-dimensional vector, separate base-action inference, and latent caching shared by actor and critic. Original implementation descriptions and Tables 1-3 retain their settings.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations for RL-100 and LIBERO and replaces the NIST webpage reference with Kimble et al. (2020). Related work more precisely distinguishes policy-gradient and reward-weighted approaches, removes the blanket costly/brittle characterization, and clarifies ResFit's lack of chunked Q learning. Overall positioning is retained.

P1.justification: Changes include a localized related-work rewrite, the new multitask/VLA appendix, updated cross-references, corrected running-header terminology, and conference/acknowledgment formatting. The main narrative and existing appendix explanations remain largely verbatim.

P2.justification: V2 adds four LIBERO figures showing aggregate and per-task results, while retaining the original graphical content and table structures. Existing appendix figures are renumbered and repositioned, Algorithm 1 moves, and Figure 7's caption replaces the misleading matched-initial-success description with the pretrained-policy comparison actually shown.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens evidence for multitask and VLA applicability through LIBERO-10 experiments and documents the π0 interface, extending v1's individual-task validation. It also corrects the misleading Figure 7 caption and refines related-work descriptions. The gain is limited by sparse statistical documentation for the new experiments and an unchanged conclusion that still presents multitask VLA finetuning as future work.
